args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: Release v2.3.1 of checkout-api was failing health checks in production in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also marked unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. A human approver signed off on the rollback. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying, and confirm the service is healthy on v2.3.0.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also failed health checks in staging before it went out.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. A human approver signed off on the rollback.
- **Result:** All three regions now run v2.3.0. Health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure and the rollback, and lists two follow-ups: find the root cause before redeploying v2.3.1, and confirm the service stays healthy on v2.3.0.

The release went to production even though its release candidate had already failed in staging. That's worth raising in the incident review.
